title: Optical cortico-cortical evoked potentials reveal structural and state-dependent cortical communication
title_zh: 光学皮层-皮层诱发电位揭示结构与状态相关的皮层通信
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cortico-cortical evoked potentials probe causal cortical communication in humans; however, establishing a preclinical methodological counterpart that combines cortex-wide coverage, high temporal resolution, minimal invasiveness, and awake-state recording remains challenging. OBJECTIVE: To map causal cortical communication and determine how local excitability, anatomical connectivity, and brain state jointly shape signal propagation across the cortex. METHODS: We used an all-optical platform that combines single-pulse transcranial optogenetic stimulation with widefield calcium imaging in awake mice, enabling stimulation and recording of cortex-wide responses from multiple motor, sensory, and association areas. We then related the spatiotemporal structure of these responses to local excitability, mesoscale functional organization, anatomical projection strength, and graded anesthesia. RESULTS: Optical Cortico-Cortical Evoked Potentials uncovered a consistent two-stage pattern of cortical communication. An initial response propagated along the anatomical scaffold linking the stimulated site to its direct targets, indicating that structural connectivity constrains the earliest phase of signal transmission. This was followed by a later, more distributed phase that varied across stimulation sites and was more sensitive to brain state, consistent with recurrent network-level integration. Across regions, stronger local recruitment was associated with broader cortex-wide engagement, suggesting that local excitability helps govern the scale of effective connectivity. CONCLUSIONS: These findings establish oCCEPs as a scalable approach for causal mapping of cortical dynamics and support a two-stage principle of cortical communication: an early structurally constrained phase followed by a later state-dependent integrative phase.
abstract_zh: 背景：皮层-皮层诱发电位（cortico‑cortical evoked potentials, CCEP）用于探测人类皮层间因果通信；然而，建立一种兼具全皮层覆盖、高时间分辨率、最小侵入性和清醒状态记录的临床前方法仍具挑战性。目的：绘制因果皮层通信图谱，并确定局部兴奋性、解剖连通性与脑状态如何共同塑造信号在皮层中的传播。方法：我们采用全光学平台，将单脉冲经颅光遗传刺激与全场钙离子成像相结合，在清醒小鼠中实现对多条运动、感觉和联想区的皮层全覆盖刺激与记录。随后将这些响应的时空结构与局部兴奋性、mesoscale功能组织、解剖投射强度以及分级麻醉水平相关联。结果：光学皮层-皮层诱发电位（oCCEP）揭示了皮层通信的两阶段一致模式。初始响应沿着将刺激部位与其直接靶点连接的解剖支架传播，表明结构连通性限制了信号传输的最早阶段。随后出现更分布式的后期阶段，其随刺激部位变化而不同，并对脑状态更敏感，符合递归网络层级整合。不同区域中，局部招募越强，皮层全覆盖的参与度越广，提示局部兴奋性有助于调控有效连通性的尺度。结论：这些发现确立了oCCEP作为可扩展的因果皮层动力学映射方法，并支持皮层通信的两阶段原则：早期受结构限制的阶段，随后是后期受状态影响的整合阶段。
